## Highlights

- **Keep your own rules next to a managed pack.**
  `scanner.sigma_local_rules_paths` and `scanner.yara_local_rules_paths` load local rule directories after the pack at startup, on reload, in `replay`, and in `doctor`.
  `rules install` and `rules update` leave them untouched, and a local rule with the same Sigma `id` or YARA name replaces the pack rule, with a warning and a `doctor` check.
  `rules update` now reuses the catalog URL recorded at install time.
- **Run integrations without root.**
  `security.integration_group` lets an unprivileged integration such as Radegast edit the configuration in place and read logs, on Unix by group and on Windows by service account.
  `security.integration_rules_directory` delegates a single rules directory the same way.
  On Windows, folders under `C:\Program Files` are no longer refused for being owned by TrustedInstaller.
- **More trustworthy diagnostics and captures.**
  `rustinel doctor` reports a missing, unreadable, corrupt, or stale telemetry snapshot instead of a passing check.
  Windows captures keep the acting process ID and image for registry, file, DNS, PowerShell, and image-load events, and PowerShell script blocks keep `MessageNumber` and `MessageTotal` so fragments can be told from whole scripts.
- **Fewer silent gaps in detection.**
  Windows memory scans now include pages that carry modifier bits such as `PAGE_NOCACHE` or `PAGE_WRITECOMBINE`.
  On macOS, network capture picks up new interfaces without a restart and restarts failed BPF workers with backoff.
- **Smoother first runs.**
  Portable packages no longer ship an empty `logs` directory that `sudo ./rustinel run` rejected, and `install.sh` prints a working command to read restricted alerts.

## Upgrade notes

- **Updating:** run `rustinel update` or install `1.9.1` explicitly with the installer version option.
  Restart the service after replacing the binary, then run `rustinel doctor`.
- **`capture` and `replay --output` refuse to overwrite.**
  An existing capture payload, manifest, or replay report now stops the command instead of being replaced.
  Remove or rename the old files, or choose a new path, in scripts that reuse output locations.
- **`doctor` can now warn where it used to pass.**
  A running service with a missing or stale telemetry snapshot exits 1, and `--json` gains a `telemetry_snapshot` entry.
  Check monitoring that treats any nonzero exit as a failure.
- **Integration access is opt-in.**
  The new `security.*` options are file-only, require a restart, and cannot be set through environment variables.
  Defaults are unchanged, and each option delegates control of the configuration or rules to that group or account, so grant it deliberately.
- **Portable first run:** if an earlier run left a user-owned `logs` directory, remove it or rerun the installer with `--force`.
- **Alert fields:** Windows PowerShell script-block alerts add `edr.powershell.message_number` and `edr.powershell.message_total`.
  Older captures without them still replay.
